newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson soars, but other Swedish shares end down.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson soars, but other Swedish shares end down.

text.p: The Swedish stockmarket ended slightly lower on Thursday as losses wiped out a seven percent jump by telecoms group LM Ericsson.

Ericsson clearly stole the show, soaring 41 crowns after posting its stronger-than-expected first-half earnings before profit-takers emerged and pushed the share to its closing price of 353 crowns, up 24, a record high.
"The sales were about 10 percent better than we expected. We will probably raise our EPS estimates by about 10 percent for 1997," said Lehman Brothers analyst Jeremy Alun-Jones.
Other blue-chips ended down. Volvo fell 4.5 crowns to 214.5.
Drug company Astra fell 5.5 crowns to 148.
Smaller information technology companies such as Frontec were in focus. It ended six crowns higher at 79.
The forestry sector index fell two percent.
Telecoms operator Europolitan posted a half-year profit of 169 million crowns compared to a loss of 164 million in the same 1996 period, sending the share down six crowns to 189 by session end.
The general index edged down 0.08 percent to 3,170.41 in heavy turnover totalling 5.8 billion crowns.
